question: What did the historian Thomas Kuhn mean by 'normal science'?
answer: The everyday work of scientists solving puzzles within an accepted framework, which he called a paradigm. Most science, Kuhn argued, extends theories rather than overturning them, and scientists trained in a paradigm take its assumptions for granted, which makes them productive, and also slow to see its flaws.
move: Shared assumptions make progress possible, and hide their own flaws.
simply: Most scientists spend their days solving puzzles inside a big accepted theory. They don't question the theory itself, until it starts to crack.
why: Every field, office and family has its normal science: rules nobody questions. Noticing yours helps you see what you might be missing.
